title: OpenAI Chat Completions compatibility adapter: request/response mapping
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a compatibility layer that accepts OpenAI Chat Completions (v1/chat/completions) requests and returns responses shaped like OpenAI, while forwarding behavior to Redwood's native API/runtime. This ticket covers the request -> internal mapping, streaming semantics, function/tool-calling behavior, and response shaping (including usage/finish_reason).

Summary of mapping decisions (high-level):
- message roles: map OpenAI roles (system/user/assistant) to Redwood's message role enum directly. Preserve 'user' field if present for telemetry but do not use for auth.
- system/instruction: treat the first system message as Redwood explicit system override; if customer includes multiple system messages, concatenate with clear separators and set a warning in warnings header.
- max_tokens / temperature / top_p / n: map directly to Redwood generation config (max_output_tokens, temperature, top_p, candidate_count). 'n' > 1 will use Redwood's candidate_count and trigger additional latency/cost signals in telemetry.
- stop sequences: translate to Redwood stop token sequences; when combined with structured output constraints (see below), stop semantics are applied after highest-precedence structured constraint.
- streaming: OpenAI streaming produces server-sent events with 'delta' fragments and occasional 'role' or 'function_call' deltas. Redwood streaming emits chunked JSON deltas; the adapter will transform Redwood chunks into OpenAI-style SSE events (data: {"id":..., "object":"chat.completion.chunk", "choices":[{...}]}) including partial 'delta' fields. We will maintain order and ensure token-level suffixes align. Implement a small buffer to coalesce very small fragments to reduce event noise (configurable, default 40ms / 3 tokens).
- function/tool calling: map OpenAI 'functions' schema to Redwood's function registry entries by name. When Redwood requests a function call, the adapter must synthesize an OpenAI-style 'function_call' object with name and arguments (JSON string). For the reverse path (user provided function responses), map back to Redwood's tool invocation payload. Support both explicit 'function_call': {"name":...} and 'auto' behavior.
- structured outputs: adopt Redwood's structured-output validators where the OpenAI response requires JSON. For chat completions that include an instruction to return JSON, we set Redwood's structured_output schema and failure-retry policy. If the model returns non-conforming output, reply with finish_reason="invalid_output" and include a standardized 'validation' field in the usage metadata.
- usage/metrics: synthesize OpenAI-like 'usage' token counts (prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens) from Redwood counters, and include additional 'redwood_extra' telemetry in HTTP headers (not in body) to avoid violating OpenAI contract shape.
- errors and finish_reason mapping: map Redwood internal finish_reasons to OpenAI finish_reasons: e.g. 'stop'->'stop', 'max_tokens'->'length', 'timeout'->'content_filter' or 'length' depending on cause, 'model_error'->'null'. Explicit mapping table will live in the spec doc linked in comments.

Edge cases and trade-offs:
- Role deltas in streaming may arrive after initial tokens; we will emit the 'role' in the first chunk where assistant text appears to match OpenAI behavior. This requires buffering initial tokens until role is known.
- Multi-function call in a single response: OpenAI historically supports one function call per choice; Redwood runtime can produce nested tool calls. We will flatten to the first function_call in the chain and include a 'redwood_function_trace' header with the full call sequence for debugging.
- Backward compatibility: we will support the current dominant OpenAI fields; unknown fields will be forwarded as 'experimental' headers to the backend so customers that rely on extensions aren't broken by dropping fields silently.

Acceptance criteria:
- POST /v1/chat/completions (compat adapter) accepts valid OpenAI chat payloads and returns responses matching OpenAI shape for the 95% of common calls used by customers (streaming and non-streaming).
- Streaming SSE event shape validated against an integration test harness that compares the adapter vs a reference node-based streamer.
- Function calling wired end-to-end with a mocked function registry and unit tests for name/args mapping and error returns.
- Structured output validation has tests for success, invalid JSON, and partial / truncated payloads.
- Usage metrics reported and verified in the telemetry dashboard (link in comments).

Notes on rollout and versioning:
- This adapter will initially be opt-in via a header X-Compat-Mode=openai (beta). After a 4-week dogfood period and couple of enterprise tests, we may make it a first-class endpoint with stricter SLAs.
- Document the differences and known incompatibilities in /docs/openai-compat.md and add migration section to Redwood Console.

Security / privacy: The adapter must not send any additional PII to outside telemetry beyond what customers already provide. Function schemas must not be auto-executed without explicit allowlist on Dedicated/Private deployments.

Implementation pointers: See the spec PR and test harness for concrete payload transforms and sample mapping tables.
